value.actual_behavior:
Read at 2026-09-07T08:00Z. stats reports awards_recorded 36,
awards_recorded_total 36000.0, payouts_recorded 2, total_paid 2000.0 and
valid_reports 40. The leaderboard lists 2 hunters, which matches
active_hunters 2, and both show total_earned 0.0; their valid_reports sum to
21, not 40.
value.description:
Which of the numbers is right is not something we can tell from outside, and
this report does not try. It asserts only that the programme agrees with
itself, the same way #68 was about a row not contradicting itself. Correct any
one of them and it goes green.
Two independent disagreements, so it is unlikely to be one field being
misread. First: whatever total_earned means -- awarded or paid -- a programme
that has recorded 36 awards and 2 payouts cannot show 0.0 for every hunter it
has, and the leaderboard lists as many hunters as active_hunters says exist.
Second: the same two endpoints disagree about how many reports are valid, 21
against 40, which no reading of total_earned explains.
A question rather than a claim, since you can see the ledger and we cannot:
what moves a row from reward_amount to actually paid? Our own 31 rows carry
reward_amount 1000.0 on 25 of them and paid_at null on every one, and
program_status reads live, so we are trying to work out whether that is a
queue we are in, a step that needs something from us, or a figure that is not
meant to be read as an entitlement at all. Happy to be told it is the third --
the check is about the surfaces agreeing, not about the money.

MEASURED VALUES (from the live service):

  [CYM-reward-totals-disagree] stats records 36000.0 awarded and 2000.0 paid, and every one of the 2 hunter(s) on the leaderboard shows total_earned 0.0; the leaderboard lists all 2 hunter(s) and accounts for 21 valid report(s), while stats calls 40 valid
    left: {'leaderboard': [{'hunter': 'expire76', 'earned': 0.0}, {'hunter': 'Crypto42day', 'earned': 0.0}], 'board_valid_reports': 21}
    right: {'awards_recorded': 36, 'awards_recorded_total': 36000.0, 'payouts_recorded': 2, 'total_paid': 2000.0, 'valid_reports': 40}
    sources: {'stats': '/api/v1/bounty/stats', 'leaderboard': '/api/v1/bounty/leaderboard'}
    population: {'hunters_listed': 2, 'active_hunters': 2}

REPRODUCE:
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/stats (no auth): awards_recorded=36, awards_recorded_total=36000.0, payouts_recorded=2, total_paid=2000.0, valid_reports=40, active_hunters=2
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/leaderboard (no auth): 2 entries, expire76 total_earned=0.0 valid_reports=19, Crypto42day total_earned=0.0 valid_reports=2
  - 19 + 2 = 21 against stats' valid_reports=40
  - GET /api/v1/bounty/reward-tiers: program_status=live, per_verified_bug=1000.0, currency=ET10

AUTOMATED CHECKS (public repo: github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica):
  tests/rest/test_reward_totals_agree.py::test_the_reward_totals_agree_with_each_other

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: read-only
verification of the REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces. No
state-changing account action, no trading, no order placement, no deposit or
withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects are out of scope.
Every figure above was measured directly against the live service, not taken
from a document, and each finding ships with the command that reproduces it.
value.expected_behavior:
The aggregate at /api/v1/bounty/stats and the per-hunter figures at
/api/v1/bounty/leaderboard should describe the same programme: the earned
column should account for what stats says was awarded or paid, and the two
should agree on how many reports are valid.
